issues.verdictReason: data_sink_impl::put() is a different pure virtual per SEASTAR_API_LEVEL (include/seastar/core/iostream.hh:110-127); other test doubles (tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh:144) guard their put() override with #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9, but the new test_data_sink_impl::put(std::span...) is unguarded. I reproduced the failure by configuring a build with -DSeastar_API_LEVEL=7 and compiling tests/unit/rpc_test.cc.o: it fails with 'marked override but does not override' and 'invalid new-expression of abstract class type test_data_sink_impl'.
issues.scopeReason: The test file and its API-level-unguarded override are wholly new in this PR.

issues.title: New regression test never exercises stream_close()'s queue-drain wait
issues.verdictReason: sink_impl::close() (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:903-924) awaits con->send(eof_marker) to fully complete via .finally() before calling close_sink()->stream_close(), so by the time stream_close() runs, _outgoing_queue_ready is already resolved in the one path the test exercises; the queue-drain wait added at src/rpc/rpc.cc:562-570 for entries accepted just before _stream_closing is set is not covered by any assertion in the new test.
issues.scopeReason: Both the production code (the wait) and the only regression test for it were added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Test never exercises the drain half of the fix (stream_close queue wait)

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: sink_impl::close() waits for the end-of-stream send before calling close_sink(), so the queue is always empty when stream_close() runs; the test would stay green if the std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready…) wait at src/rpc/rpc.cc:562-570 were reverted.

issues.title: New test tolerates both refusal and silent acceptance of the racy send
issues.verdictReason: At this point in the test _stream_closing is already set synchronously before the mocked write_buf.close() can block (src/rpc/rpc.cc:554 runs before any suspension point), so stream_send_empty_frame() should deterministically throw closed_error; the test only catches that type instead of requiring it (e.g. via BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW), so a regression that silently accepts and queues the frame without it reaching put() before release_close.set_value() would still pass.
issues.scopeReason: The test assertion is new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Test never asserts the refusal; accepts both success and closed_error

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2016-2019 accepts both success and closed_error outcomes; the test fails only if the batch-flush poller later writes, so a regression that accepts the frame but defers or drops it would pass.

issues.title: Claim that the yield() loop doesn't drive the batch-flush poller
issues.verdictReason: yield() itself doesn't poll I/O, but each yield().get() inside a seastar::thread suspends the fiber back to the reactor's main loop (src/core/reactor.cc:3433-3442), which calls poll_once() unconditionally every iteration (src/core/reactor.cc:3539-3546), running every registered poller including batch_flush_poller (src/core/reactor.cc:3359). The 10-iteration loop therefore does give the batch flush poller real chances to run, matching the comment's intent.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new in this PR, even though the verdict is that it is not actually wrong.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: "Let the batch flush poller run" comment is wrong; yield() doesn't poll for I/O

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: yield() queues a task and does not poll for I/O (include/seastar/util/later.hh:41-44), so the loop doesn't run the poller; on base, detection depends on later .get() calls happening to poll, otherwise on the destructor assert.

issues.title: New test can hang or SIGABRT instead of failing cleanly on a regression
issues.verdictReason: SEASTAR_ASSERT is active in all build modes (include/seastar/util/assert.hh:29-36) and ~sink_impl() asserts sink_closed() (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:931-936); the test doesn't use deferred_close(sink) the way later tests in the same file do (tests/unit/rpc_test.cc:2131,2158), so an earlier BOOST_REQUIRE failure (e.g. at line 2000) unwinds through an unclosed sink and aborts the process. Separately, catching only rpc::closed_error around stream_send_empty_frame().get() means any other exception type skips st.release_close.set_value(), leaving test_data_sink_impl::close() parked forever.
issues.scopeReason: The test's exception-safety gaps are new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Test failures hang or abort instead of reporting cleanly

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: close_entered_cv.wait at :2011 has no timeout; if BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL at :2000 fails, the sink is dropped unclosed and ~sink_impl's SEASTAR_ASSERT aborts the process; if the hook throws anything other than closed_error, release_close is never set; existing stream tests avoid this with deferred_close(sink).

issues.title: Cross-shard data race on hook_capturing_compressor_factory::hooks vector
issues.verdictReason: negotiate() does const_cast + hooks.push_back() with no synchronization, and is invoked per-connection on whichever shard the connection lands on. I built the PR and ran test_stream_send_after_stream_close repeatedly with -- -c 2 (matching this project's documented default --smp of 2 for test.py): it crashed or threw an unexpected seastar::rpc::stream_closed exception in roughly 1 in 8 runs, consistent with heap corruption from concurrent push_back on the shared server_factory.hooks vector across shards; it never failed over 40+ runs at -c 1.
issues.scopeReason: The racy helper class is new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Cross-shard data race in hook_capturing_compressor_factory::negotiate

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: negotiate (:1957) pushes into one shard-0 std::vector; with -c 2, loopback round-robin accepts the parent connection on shard 0 and the stream connection on shard 1, so both server-side negotiations write to it unsynchronized; recording only when !is_server fixes it since server hooks are never used.

issues.title: New comment misstates when _outgoing_queue_ready becomes exceptional
issues.verdictReason: connection::send()'s continuation (src/rpc/rpc.cc:333-338) calls abort() on a failed send_entry() but then unconditionally calls p->done.set_value() (not set_exception), so a failed send does not make the chained _outgoing_queue_ready future exceptional; it only becomes exceptional via withdraw()'s ex path during stop_send_loop(). The code is harmless either way since f.ignore_ready_future() handles both cases.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: New comment misstates the cause of _outgoing_queue_ready becoming exceptional

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: src/rpc/rpc.cc:566-567 says _outgoing_queue_ready "is exceptional if an entry failed," but a failed send_entry calls abort() and then p->done.set_value() (:333-338); the future only becomes exceptional through stop_send_loop while _negotiated is still pending. The code itself is harmless.

issues.title: New rpc_types.hh doc overstates that an unmarshall exception always closes the source
issues.verdictReason: source_impl::operator()'s fast path (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:940-947) calls unmarshall() directly on already-buffered data; if it throws, the exception propagates synchronously without ever calling close_source(), unlike the refill path which does call close_source() on failure (rpc_impl.hh:957-960). So 'reading until it throws... closes it' is not true for every throw, and an application that stops reading after such an exception leaves the source open, which is exactly the leak the new docs warn about.
issues.scopeReason: This doc paragraph is new in this PR, even though the underlying source_impl code is untouched.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Docs wrongly claim reading a source until it throws always closes it

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:384-389 and doc/rpc-streaming.md:110-112 say reading a source until it throws closes it, but an unmarshall exception in source_impl::operator() (rpc_impl.hh:948) propagates without close_source(); an application that stops reading after never triggers stream_close(), which is the leak these docs warn about.

issues.title: New doc overstates that the stream connection shuts down 'only once' both halves close
issues.verdictReason: client::abort_all_streams() and server::connection::abort_all_streams() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:848,1324, called from the stop paths at :1072 and :1295) also tear down stream connections, independent of stream_check_twoway_closed(); the connection can likewise go down on peer EOF or error. 'only once both halves are closed' omits these paths.
issues.scopeReason: This sentence is new text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Docs overstate that the connection is shut down "only once" both halves are closed

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: doc/rpc-streaming.md:115 says the connection is shut down only once both halves are closed, but it is also shut down on peer EOF, on error, and through abort_all_streams.

issues.title: New doc understates dropping an unclosed sink as merely 'an error'
issues.verdictReason: ~sink_impl() calls SEASTAR_ASSERT(sink_closed()), and SEASTAR_ASSERT is active in all build modes and calls assert_fail(), which aborts the process (include/seastar/util/assert.hh:29-36, include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:931-936) -- not a recoverable 'error' as the wording implies.
issues.scopeReason: This doc sentence is new text added by this PR.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-claude-retest-2026-10-09/iro: doc/rpc-streaming.md:109 says "Dropping an unclosed sink is an error," but it is an always-on SEASTAR_ASSERT that aborts the process.
